mu_name_from: MuMain loads helm indexes 10 to 14 from HelmElf{i+1} (ZzzOpenData.cpp line 148: `AccessModel(MODEL_HELM + i + 10, ..., L"HelmElf", i + 1)`), so index 12 is HelmElf03, which openmu's 0.75 Armors.cs names the Wind Helm. Group 7 index 12, Player/HelmElf03.bmd.
why_this_one: The Fairy Elf's third set, sold beside Silk: Elf Lala in Noria carries all five pieces at +3 (src/sim/market.cpp, kElfLala, the index-12 rows). Here so that her shelf shows the pieces it sells rather than their names.
profile_from: Not armour, whose default is plate_steel: nothing in this set is a forged plate. The sheets are blue quilted fabric with a darker blue scroll worked into it, no metal colour anywhere but the Armor's two tan straps. See profiles/soft_armour.json.
keeps_head_from: ZzzCharacter.cpp line 12122, SetCharacterScale: helms MODEL_VINE_HELM to MODEL_SPIRIT_HELM keep BODYPART_HEAD as the class's bare head and draw it under the helm, and helm 12 is inside that range (10 Vine, 11 Silk, 12 Wind, 13 Spirit). The model agrees: one sheet, 38 triangles, no skin sheet, so it carries no face of its own. See HelmElf01's note for the whole rule.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Armors.cs line 65. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: ArmorInitializerBase.CreateArmor(number, slot, width, height, name, dropLevel, defense, durability, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, darkWizardClassLevel, darkKnightClassLevel, elfClassLevel). `armor.Group = (byte)(slot + 5)`, so slot 2 is group 7, 3 is 8 and 4 is 9.
stats.defense_note: Points of defence, in the row and summed into Player.ArmourDefense by Wear - see shared/Rows.cs.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are 0, 0, 1 - the Fairy Elf alone. 80 agility beside thirty strength is the row saying the same thing in stats.

sheet_from: Data/Player/head_a03.OZJ (64x64), from MuMain, and it is the only sheet the model names - one mesh, 38 triangles, no hide and no skin. The .bmd names head_a03.jpg.
sheet_note: head_a03 is a blue fabric hood swept back like a blown scarf, a darker blue scroll worked into it and a pale ground where the sheet is unused. Mean (75, 99, 137) at chroma 62.
material_note: Three islands, 6, 16 and 16 - head_a03's 38 and nothing else: the hood and its two swept tails. All cloth over the profile's leather: blue quilted fabric with the scroll painted into it, no plate and no metal colour anywhere on the sheet.
